state.target_treatment: Independent pre-selection culture growth histories and the interpretation of resistance after phage selection.
state.scope: Table 1 experiment 11a versus Table 2 experiment 11, with the source's mutation-and-clonal-growth interpretation. Other experiment columns and mutation-rate estimation are excluded.

evidence.location: Printed pp. 502-504 (PDF pp. 12-14), plating methods, Table 1 and Table 2
evidence.text: Table 1 uses parallel platings of samples from the same grown culture to check sampling and plating variability. Table 2 uses cultures grown separately in parallel before testing. In experiment 11a the ten resistant-colony counts are 46, 56, 52, 48, 65, 44, 49, 51, 56, 47. In experiment 11 they are 30, 10, 40, 45, 183, 12, 173, 23, 57, 51.

Under the mutation interpretation, resistance can arise before virus exposure and be inherited by descendants. Early mutations can therefore contribute many resistant cells. The paper distinguishes mutation events from their descendants and interprets the fluctuations using clonal relatedness. Neither selected table assigns colonies to individual mutation origins.

records.record_origin: Original row order checked visually in both scanned tables. Experiment 11a and 11 are distinct source labels; row indices identify samples or cultures according to the table.

criteria.one_origin_per_cell: Each resistant cell necessarily represents a different mutation origin.
criteria.clonal_descendants: Several resistant cells can descend from one earlier resistance mutation; cell or colony abundance does not identify the number of origins.
criteria.selection_creates_each_origin: Each resistant cell acquires a new resistance mutation only when virus is added, independently of pre-selection ancestry.
criteria.repeated_image: The reported colonies are repeated images of one physical colony, with no distinct resistant cells.
